features.title: Fixed Asset Master Data Management
features.description: Enables fixed asset managers to search for fixed asset records by code and name, insert new records, update existing entries, delete selected rows, copy rows, clear search criteria, print asset data, export to Excel, and close the window. The interface provides a DataWindow grid for data display and a toolbar of command buttons for all operations.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint w_fa_ances_infree (Fixed Asset Data Entry), S.5 Events #1-#9

functions.label: Search fixed asset records and display results (Search)
functions.description: The user initiates a search for fixed asset master data based on provided criteria. The system executes the query and populates the grid with matching records. This allows the user to locate specific assets for review or update.

functions.label: Add a new fixed asset row to the grid (Row Insert)
functions.description: The user can insert a new empty row into the grid to start creating a fixed asset record. This operation happens in the client buffer and enables the copy and delete buttons for subsequent actions. It supports efficient data entry for new assets.

functions.label: Delete selected fixed asset row from grid (Row Delete)
functions.description: The user selects a row and deletes it from the grid's client buffer. The deletion is synchronous and disables the copy and delete buttons if no rows remain. This provides a way to remove erroneous or unwanted entries before saving.

functions.label: Copy a selected fixed asset row (Row Copy)
functions.description: The user can initiate copying of a selected row in the grid. The actual duplication logic is deferred to descendant windows, so the base form contains only a placeholder for this action. This allows customization of copy behavior for specific asset types.

functions.label: Save changes to fixed asset records (Update)
functions.description: The user triggers a save operation for all modifications made in the grid. The system validates data integrity with null and update checks before persisting changes to the database, then shows a confirmation. This ensures reliable data storage.

functions.label: Print fixed asset grid data (Print)
functions.description: The user can print the currently displayed grid contents. The system confirms the action, prints the data, and locks the MDI interface during printing to prevent data changes. This provides a physical record or audit trail.

functions.label: Export fixed asset grid to Excel or CSV (Excel)
functions.description: The user can export the grid data to an Excel or CSV file for further analysis. The system uses a standard save function to create the file on the client side. This enables data sharing and reporting outside the application.

functions.label: Reset grid and search parameters (Clear)
functions.description: The user can clear all search criteria and reset the displayed grid to an empty state. The system hides data, clears retrieval flags, and re-binds the transaction for a fresh session. This prepares the interface for a new query or data entry cycle.

functions.label: Close the asset management window (Close)
functions.description: The user closes the fixed asset master data window. The system triggers a close event that rolls back any uncommitted FATRA transaction, ensuring data consistency. This provides a safe and clean exit from the module.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder MDI child window (w_fa_ances_infree) where fixed asset managers search for fixed asset records by code and name, maintain master data (insert, update, delete, copy) via a DataWindow grid (dw_ances), and perform auxiliary operations (clear, print, export, close) using command buttons.
business_context.target_state: A React fixed asset management page (<FixedAssetManager />) backed by REST microservices (GET /api/v1/fixed-assets, POST /api/v1/fixed-assets, PUT /api/v1/fixed-assets/{id}, DELETE /api/v1/fixed-assets/{id}) with inline grid editing, export to Excel, and print capabilities.

user_stories.title: Save Fixed Asset Record Changes
user_stories.i_want_to: save all modifications (edits, new rows, deletions) to the fixed asset master data by clicking the Update button
user_stories.so_that: I can persistently record my master data updates.

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has edited an existing asset record's field with valid data
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks Update and confirms the action
acceptance_criteria.then: the system persists the changes, resets the grid to a clean state, and shows a success confirmation

acceptance_criteria.given: the user leaves a required field blank in any modified row
acceptance_criteria.then: the system highlights the empty required field, displays the error '必須情報が入力されていません。', and cancels the update

acceptance_criteria.given: the user inserts a new row and fills in all required fields
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks Update and confirms
acceptance_criteria.then: the new asset record is created in the database and the grid resets

acceptance_criteria.given: the user deletes an existing row from the grid
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks Update and confirms
acceptance_criteria.then: the corresponding asset record is removed from the database and the grid resets

acceptance_criteria.given: the user copies a row (via descendant implementation)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks Update and confirms
acceptance_criteria.then: the copied record is persisted as a new asset

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: cb_update.clicked triggers u_nullchek, u_updtchek, u_update. DataWindow dw_data uses FATRA transaction; rollback on close. Global functions f_delete, f_insert used for row ops.
user_stories.migration_hint: PUT /api/v1/fixed-assets (bulk update with optimistic locking). React inline grid editing with AutoSave or explicit Update button.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All update operations must execute within an atomic database transaction with rollback on any error.

user_stories.migration_hint: React: window close via tab/browser navigation or a close button with confirmation dialog before discarding changes.
